pages.text: After shearing, leftover wool lay piled in the yard. Soft and fluffy, like clouds.
"I will make a ball to play with the lamb." Pipo gathered a handful.
Mrs. Goose stretched her neck to interfere. "The bigger the ball, the better! Everyone says so!"
Whenever Pipo packed the wool, she added more. The lump grew bigger than his head.
"More, more! Those children's ball was this big!" The lump grew as big as Pipo.
He pressed hard, and poof—the whole lump came apart.
Wool covered the yard. Covered in wool too, Mrs. Goose sneezed. "Achoo!"
Pipo gathered just one handful again. He packed it firmly with both hands.
It became a small, solid ball. A tap sent it rolling.
The lamb nudged the ball with its nose to play. Pipo bounced along too. Mrs. Goose was making her own ball from leftover wool. "I will make one too."
